decisions.reason: As the surviving process-data software after A was withdrawn, it benefits from prior development effort, fits the firm's data-driven direction, and any weak visibility can still be explained by integration into broader system offers.

Its earlier standalone web presentation and fit with the established infrastructure portfolio create some commitment to continue, although its weaker link to the firm's digital strategic thrust raises the risk of later withdrawal.

With only limited public commitment, a more niche mechanical role, and a weaker connection to the firm's announced move toward connected and data-driven infrastructure management, this is the product most likely to be discontinued.

Control technology for water engineering machinery is central to the firm's core business and strategic move toward connected operations, so sunk development effort and strategic fit strongly favor continuation.

As a newer product with its own page and a close match to automation, measurement, and system software capabilities, management would be inclined to persist and attribute any slower uptake to long infrastructure sales cycles rather than to product failure.
